title: Tsunami Coastal Safety & Evacuation Guide
summary: Tsunamis are series of massive ocean waves caused by undersea earthquakes. Move inland and to high ground immediately.
precautions: If you feel a strong coastal earthquake or see sudden ocean drawback (water receding rapidly exposing sea floor), MOVE INLAND IMMEDIATELY.
Do NOT wait for official warning sirens if natural warning signs are observed.
Tsunamis consist of multiple wave surges over several hours; the first wave is rarely the largest.
evacuation: Move inland at least 2-3 km or climb to an elevation of at least 30 meters (100 feet) above sea level.
If trapped, climb to upper floors or roof of a reinforced concrete high-rise building.
Abandon vehicles if traffic grinds to a halt; proceed on foot up hill slopes.
firstAid: Administer CPR to drowning victims immediately.
Treat salt-water aspiration and hypothermia with dry clothing, warmth, and oxygen.
Clean debris wounds to prevent sea-water bacterial infections.
emergencyChecklist: Go-Bag with water, food, and medicines
dos: DO move to high ground immediately after coastal shaking.
DO stay away from beaches and coastal inlets.
DO wait for official 'All Clear' before returning.
donts: DON'T go down to the beach to watch the tsunami wave.
DON'T return after the first wave passes.
